projects.title: accessibility - Missing Surface Materials
projects.description: We're filling up the remaining surface=* tags, mainly for accessibility and oswm

projects.title: Milan - Cycleway Missing Foot Tags
projects.description:
This challenge identifies all cycleways that are missing
information about access permission for pedestrians. Mappers are asked to add a foot tag to the
cycleway to clearly identify whether foot traffic is allowed on the cycleway. Please see [Examples
from the highway=cycleway wiki page](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:highway%3Dcycleway#Examples)
to learn more about how to add a foot tag to the cycleway.

projects.title: Milan - Fix Conflicting Crossing Feature Tags
projects.description:
This challenge is designed to assist OpenStreetMap contributors in identifying and resolving conflicts in tags associated with crossing ways and nodes. Both crossing ways and nodes may have tags that indicate whether the crossing is marked or unmarked, the type of marking, and the presence of traffic signals. Each task within this challenge pinpoints a pair of crossing way and crossing node that have conflicting tags.
To resolve these conflicts, please use aerial imagery to determine which tags should be retained and which should be modified. We recommend using the Rapid editor for making changes, as this tool has built-in validation tests that will simplify this process.
Please exercise caution when considering the deletion of tags. Only remove a tag if you are completely sure that it is incorrect. Your contributions are valuable in maintaining the accuracy and usefulness of OpenStreetMap. Thank you for your efforts.

projects.title: Milan - Missing Crossing Way
projects.description:
This challenge focuses on identifying
crossing nodes that are not connected to a crossing way. A crossing *node* is
a specific type of node that indicates where pedestrian or bicycle crossings
intersect with roads. A crossing *way*, on the other hand, represents the
physical crossing itself, such as a lined or zebra crossing.

Typically, a crossing node should connect to both a highway and a footway
or cycleway. However, we have found instances where crossing nodes are either
incorrectly tagged or not connected to any crossing highway. Each task flags
an instance of a crossing node that is not connected to a crossing way.

We ask that mappers working on these tasks use satellite imagery to identify
the crossing node and its connection to the highway. If the crossing node is
is mistagged, or misplaced then please resolve the issue and make sure that
the crossing node is located at the intersection of a crossing way and a
highway.

projects.title: Milan - ML Crossing Detection
projects.description:
This challenge identifies potential
pedestrian crossings that have not been mapped. We are using machine learning
to detect crosswalks from satellite imagery and then determine if an OSM
crosswalk exists at that location. When we find a crosswalk that appears not
to have been mapped yet we flag that as a Map Roulette task.

It is important to have a human review of these tasks because there are many
places where the crosswalk is not clear and human review together with street
side photos are necessary to correctly map the crossing.

It is also important to realize that we are spotting the absence of something
so when you are sent to the editor to make changes you may need to zoom in to
be able to spot the issue. We recommend using the + button to zoom in as
the area of importance will be in the center of the map.

projects.title: Milan - Sidewalks Maybe Missing
projects.description:
This challenge focuses on improving the mapping of sidewalks in OSM by tagging road segments with appropriate sidewalk tags.
Mappers should aim to tag roads with sidewalk:left, sidewalk:right, or sidewalk:both if straightforward.
If not feasible, tag the road as sidewalk:both = separate and map all footways as separate ways using highway=footway tags.
Street-level imagery is recommended to assist in mapping these footways accurately. Your contributions will enhance the quality of
OSM data and support various applications relying on this information. These are likley challenging to map from aerial imagery, we recommend using street level imagery to assist mapping these.

projects.title: Milan - Complex Intersection Footways
projects.description:
This challenge aims to enhance the mapping of footways in OSM by creating detailed geometries around intersections and connecting them to existing networks.
We are relying on human editors to review and update the map data, ensuring that it accurately reflects real-world conditions.
It is essential to have a thorough understanding of OSM tagging conventions and best practices for mapping footways.
Your contributions will help improve the overall quality of OSM data and support various applications that rely on this information. When working on these tasks, please pay close attention to the following aspects:
Create footway geometries around intersections, extending them beyond the intersection to connect with existing pedesterian networks.
Update road tags to reflect the presence of separate sidewalks using the correct sidewalk = * tag
Add sidewalk and crossing ways, indicating whether they are marked or unmarked.
Check layer tags for overpasses and ensure that footways are correctly connected across layers.
By following these guidelines, you will be contributing to a more comprehensive and accurate representation of pedestrian infrastructure in OSM.

projects.title: Milan - Non Noded Footway and Service Road Intersections
projects.description:
This challenge focuses on identifying and reviewing
cases where OSM footways intersect with service roads on the same layer but the geometries do not connect to each other. These
intersections may represent mapping issues where the relationship between the footway and service road
needs to be clarified. Mappers are asked to review these intersections verify wether or not the footway and service road should share a node.

projects.title: Milan - Validate Cycleway Foot Tag
projects.description:
This challenge focuses on verifying cycleways that are currently
tagged with foot=no or foot=private to ensure the accuracy of pedestrian access information. Mappers are asked while
reviewing these cycleways to confirm whether the foot=no or foot=private tag is appropriate or if adjustments are needed.
For guidance on using the foot tag, please refer to (https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:foot)
to learn more about how to use a foot tag.

projects.title: Milan - OSM Footways That Are Potential Sidewalks
projects.description:
This project aims to review OpenStreetMap (OSM) footways that potentially are sidewalks due to proximity to their road but missing the correct footway=* tag.
The primary goal is to add footway=sidewalk where appropriate. If the footway is not a sidewalk, consider adding footway=path or marking the task as not an issue depending on local OSM editing conventions.
Please review the footway and confirm if it is a sidewalk, pathway, or something else.
Consider street level imagery to help with this task.
Each challenge involves a footway that may be a sidewalk due to their proximity to the road.
Our goal is to ensure accurate representation of sidewalks in OSM.
Your contributions will enhance the quality of OSM data and support various applications relying on this information.

projects.title: Milan - Residential Road Foot No tags
projects.description:
This challenge focuses on reviewing and correcting the usage of foot=no tags on residential roads in OSM.
Mappers should aim to verify if the foot=no tag is correctly used, reserving it for cases where access on
foot or by pedestrians is prohibited (private roads) or obviously dangerous for foot traffic (like when a residential road meets a divided highway)
If not valid, update the sidewalk:both tag instead or use sidewalk:left/right when appropriate.
Aerial and street-level imagery are recommended to assist in verifying these tags accurately.
Your contributions will enhance the quality of OSM data and support various applications relying on this information.

projects.title: Milan - Untagged Crossing Ways
projects.description:
This challenge is all about finding
crossing ways that are missing a crossing tag. A crossing tag tells us
whether the crossing is marked or unmarked. For example, if the crossing
is a zebra crossing, the crossing tag would be zebra - thats my
favorite kind of crossing!

Its important to tag crossing ways with a crossing tag so that other
map users know what type of crossing it is and what markings to expect.
That way, they can stay safe and cross the road safely.

This challenge will help us identify crossing ways that are missing a
crossing tag so that we can fix them. We are going to use satellite
imagery to see if we can tell whether the crossing is marked or unmarked.
If we can, we will add a crossing tag to the crossing way.

But if we can not tell from the satellite imagery whether the crossing is
marked or unmarked, we will leave the crossing way untagged. Its better
to leave a crossing way untagged than to add a wrong crossing tag.

So, if you are up for a challenge, join us in our quest to make all crossing
ways safe and accessible for everyone. Crikey, its going to be a beaut!

projects.title: Milan - Review Possible Mistagged Unmarked Crossing Ways
projects.description:
Welcome to the Map Roulette
project for reviewing potentially mistagged pedestrian crossing ways! Our
goal is to improve the accuracy of OpenStreetMap data by verifying and
updating the tags for crosswalks that may be mislabeled as unmarked.

Using machine learning, we have identified potential mistagged crossings
that are labeled as 'unmarked' in OSM but may actually be marked. Your task
is to review these crossings and update their tags to include the proper
'crossing' and 'crossing:markings' tags.

Please note that some of these tasks may be false positives, so it's important
to carefully review each case. If a marking appears unmarked across various
satellite imagery, mark it as 'Not An Issue'. Additionally, keep in mind that
some crossings may have been recently marked, so be sure to check different
satellite imagery layers/sources with the latest capture date to verify.

By participating in this challenge, you will be contributing to the
improvement of OpenStreetMap data and helping to make all crossing ways
safe and accessible for everyone. So, if you're up for a challenge, join
us in our quest to create more accurate maps!

projects.title: Milan - Suspicious Unmarked Crossing Ways
projects.description:
The goal of this challenge is to identify and improve the mapping of unmarked crossings on busy or high-traffic roads.
Unmarked crossings can be dangerous for pedestrians and other non-motorized road users, as they may not be easily visible to drivers.
By identifying and improving the mapping of these crossings, we can help make our streets safer and more accessible for everyone.
Task Description:
For this challenge, we will be focusing on ways that are tagged as crossing=unmarked and cross busy or potentially high traffic roads.
Your task is to verify that these crossings exist and are accurately mapped in OpenStreetMap. If the crossing does not exist or is not accurately mapped, please make the necessary changes to the map.
To complete this challenge, verify that an actual crossing exists as represented by the OSM feature and that it is accurately tagged.
If the crossing does not exist or is not accurately mapped, make the necessary changes to the map.
- If the crossing exists (there are curb cuts or other indications) and there are no markings, you may leave the crossing as is.
- If the crossing exists and is indicated by different surface types, change the crossing tag to crossing=marked and add a crossing:markings=surface tag.
- If the crossing exists and is marked, change the crossing tag to marked, uncontrolled, or traffic_signals as appropriate.
- If no formal crossing exists but it looks like a place where people cross the road, change the crossing tag to crossing=informal and change the highway tag to something other than crossing. This helps distinguish between unmarked official crossings and informal crossings.
- If a crossing does not exist and would be dangerous for pedestrians to cross at this location, delete the crossing.

By completing tasks in this challenge, you will be helping to make OpenStreetMap more accurate and useful for pedestrians and other non-motorized road users. Good luck!

projects.title: Milan - Conflicting Crossing Tags
projects.description:
This challenge is all about finding
crossing ways that have conflicting crossing tags. That means that either
the crossing tag and crossing:markings tag do not agree with each other or
perhaps the footway tag is inconsistent with the highway tag.

For example, if the crossing tag is set to zebra, but the crossing:markings
tag is set to unmarked, that means that the crossing is tagged as both
marked and unmarked. Thats no good - have you ever seen a zebra with no
markings?!?!

This challenge will help us identify crossing ways that have conflicting
crossing tags so that we can fix them. We are going to use satellite imagery
to see if we can tell whether the crossing is marked or unmarked. If we can,
we will change the crossing tag and crossing:markings tag so that they match.

But if we can not tell from the satellite imagery whether the crossing is
marked or unmarked, we will leave the crossing tag and crossing:markings tag
as they are. Its better to leave a tag blank than to add a wrong tag.

Remember, its important to tag crossing ways correctly so that other map
users know what type of crossing it is and what markings to expect. That
way, they can stay safe and cross the road safely.

So, if you are up for a challenge, join us in our quest to make all crossing
ways safe and accessible for everyone. Crikey, its going to be a beaut!
